prompt: A stone dropped in a pond makes a circular ripple whose radius grows at $3$ cm per second. When the radius is $10$ cm, the area inside the ripple is growing at $k\pi$ square cm per second. Find $k$.
hint: Start with $A = \pi r^2$ and differentiate with respect to time. Remember the chain rule on $r^2$.

hints.text: Start with $A = \pi r^2$ and differentiate with respect to time. Remember the chain rule on $r^2$.

explanation: So $k = 60$. Unlike the circumference, the area's growth rate depends on the current radius — a bigger ripple sweeps out area faster.

alternativeExplanations.title: The thin ring picture
steps: In a short time $dt$ the ripple grows by a thin ring of width $3\,dt$ and length (circumference) $2\pi \cdot 10 = 20\pi$.
Divide by $dt$: the area grows at $60\pi$ cm$^2$/s.
